did_you_know.text: The heading identifies the psalm as a psalm of David and places its setting in the wilderness of Judah; from the very beginning, it creates a picture of a dry and isolated landscape.
The psalmist uses images of thirst and the body—“My soul thirsts for you” and “my body longs for you”—to describe the intensity of his longing for God in a land without water.
The memory of the temple or holy place, where the psalmist saw the LORD’s power and glory, serves as an answer to the spiritual thirst mentioned earlier.
The psalmist declares that the LORD’s faithful love is better than life itself, so his response is praise: “My lips will praise you.”
This verse contains a physical and tangible prayer: lifting up the hands in the LORD’s name expresses the psalmist’s blessing, appeal, and thanksgiving.

Spiritual satisfaction is described through images of a feast—“rich food and choice meat”—while praise is described as “joyful lips”; in this way, the psalm connects physical satisfaction with inner joy.
Even during the night, the psalmist remembers and meditates on the LORD; faith and prayer are not limited to daylight hours or times of activity.
The phrase “in the shadow of your wings” paints a picture of shelter and protection, and within that refuge the psalmist sings and rejoices.
The psalmist describes a close and continual relationship in the words “I cling to you,” and immediately adds that the LORD supports him with his right hand—with strength and care.
The conclusion presents two contrasting voices: the king rejoices and boasts in God, while the mouths of liars are silenced; the psalm thus ends with faith in joy and justice.
